title: Paano Magtanim ng Pechay: How to Plant Pechay the Traditional Way
metaTitle: Paano Magtanim ng Pechay: The Traditional Way, Step by Step
metaDescription: Paano magtanim ng pechay? See how traditional farmers plant petsay step by step, with the days, the spacing and what to change for a higher yield.
excerpt: Paano magtanim ng pechay? Here is how traditional Filipino farmers usually plant petsay (pechay), step by step from getting the field ready to the harvest, with the day of each step and what to change for a higher yield.

heroImage.alt: Vegetable terraces and plastic tunnels on the slopes of Mankayan, Benguet

blocks.title: This is the traditional way
blocks.text: This guide shows how traditional farmers usually plant petsay. Use it as a starting point. For a higher yield, update it: plant certified seed or clean planting material, test your soil, and follow the right spacing and fertilizer.

How Filipino vegetable farmers usually grow pechay on beds, either sown in a seedbed and moved to the field or sown straight on the bed, up to the harvest about a month later. For backyard and small market growers who want the usual routine and what to change for more and cleaner leaves.

Before you plant, get the field ready with our [land preparation guide for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation). Then choose your seed or planting material with the [petsay varieties sold here](/crop-varieties/chinese-cabbage). If the leaves turn pale later on, the [petsay nutrient deficiency guide](/nutrient-deficiencies/pechay-nutrient-deficiency) helps you find what is missing. For more on the crop, read [pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay), [vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).
When to plant petsay

Pechay grows all year in the lowlands but does best in the dry, cooler months, roughly November to April. In the rainy months farmers plant on raised beds and under light cover, because heavy rain tears the leaves and brings rot. It grows from the lowlands up to mid elevations.
What you plant

Seed, bought in small packs or cans. Farmers either sow it thinly in a seedbed or seedling tray and transplant the seedlings after two to three weeks, or broadcast or drill it straight on the bed and thin later.
Paano magtanim ng pechay: seedbed then transplant
This is the seedbed then transplant way (Seedbed then transplant (punla at lipat tanim)). The crop is ready about 25 days after transplanting.
Seedbed then transplant: before planting (Bago magtanim)

items.title: 21 days before transplanting: Plow and harrow
items.text: Plow and harrow two or three times, about a week apart, to a depth of 15 to 20 cm so the soil is fine and the weeds are gone.

items.title: 1 day before transplanting: Form the beds and put the base fertilizer
items.text: Make beds about 1 m wide with paths of 20 to 25 cm between them. Mix chicken manure and a little complete fertilizer into the bed and cover it with soil. Tip: Raise the beds higher in the rainy months so water runs off.

blocks.text: Seedbed then transplant: the nursery (Punlaan)

items.title: 18 days before transplanting: Make the seedbed and sow
items.text: Raise a seedbed about 1 m wide and 15 cm high with fine, clean soil. Sow the seed thinly in shallow lines or 2 to 3 seeds a hole in a seedling tray, cover lightly with fine soil and sprinkle with water.

parts.title: Build the bed
parts.text: Raise a bed about 1 m wide, 10 m long and 15 cm high in a sunny spot near water. Crush the clods and rake the soil until it is fine and loose.

parts.title: Clean the soil
parts.text: Spread dry rice straw over the bed and burn it, or pour boiling water over it and cover it with plastic until the soil cools. This kills the damping off fungus, weed seed and soil insects before sowing.

parts.title: Sow thinly in lines
parts.text: Water the bed first, then scratch shallow lines across it with a stick. Drop the seed thinly along the lines and cover it with a light sprinkle of fine soil.

parts.title: Or sow in a seedling tray
parts.text: Fill the tray holes with a clean potting mix and press it down lightly with the palm. Drop two or three seeds in each hole, cover them with fine soil and sprinkle with water.

parts.title: Keep it wet until they come up
parts.text: Sprinkle gently every morning or late afternoon so the top soil never dries out while the seed is sprouting. Use a can with a fine sprinkler head so the water does not wash the seed out.

items.title: 14 days before transplanting: Shade and water the seedlings
items.text: Give the young seedlings a simple roof against strong sun and hard rain, and water them in the morning or late afternoon.

items.title: 12 days before transplanting: Prick out into small pots
items.text: About five days after the seedlings come up, many growers move each one into its own small pot of rolled banana leaf, so it goes to the field with its roots in a ball of soil and does not wilt.

parts.title: Roll the banana leaf pots
parts.text: Cut banana leaf into strips, roll each strip into a small cup and fill it with the same clean soil mix used for the seedbed. Stand the pots close together in a box or on the bed.

parts.title: Lift the seedlings gently
parts.text: Loosen the seedbed soil with a small stick and lift the seedlings with a little soil on the roots. Hold them by a leaf, not by the thin stem, which bruises easily.

parts.title: One seedling a pot
parts.text: Make a hole in each pot with a finger, set one seedling in it and press the soil around it. Water the pots right away with a weak starter fertilizer mixed in water, or plain water.

parts.title: Shade them for a few days
parts.text: Keep the pots under the shed roof until the seedlings stand up again, then give them more sun each day until transplanting.

items.title: 7 days before transplanting: Harden the seedlings
items.text: Remove the cover bit by bit during the last week so the seedlings get used to full sun before they go to the field.

blocks.text: Seedbed then transplant: planting day (Pagtatanim)

items.title: Transplanting day: Transplant in the afternoon
items.text: Move seedlings that are two to three weeks old to the beds, 10 cm apart in rows 20 cm apart. Water right after planting.

blocks.text: Seedbed then transplant: care while it grows (Pag aalaga)

items.title: Day 1: Water every day
items.text: Water daily with a watering can or hose in the morning or late afternoon, enough to keep the bed moist but not soggy.

items.title: Day 5: Replace dead seedlings
items.text: Fill any gaps with spare seedlings from the seedbed during the first week.

items.title: Day 10: Side dress and weed
items.text: Many farmers give a little urea, often dissolved in water, along the rows about one to two weeks after transplanting, and pull the weeds at the same time.

items.title: Day 12: Check for pests twice a week
items.text: Look under the leaves for aphids, small holes from flea beetles and the green larvae of the diamondback moth. Pull out and bury plants with soft, smelly rot or swollen roots.

items.title: Day 25: Wash, bundle and keep cool
items.text: Wash off the soil, remove yellow leaves, tie in bundles and keep them in the shade, sprinkled with water, until they reach the market.

blocks.text: Seedbed then transplant: harvest (Anihan)

items.title: Day 25: Harvest in the cool hours
items.text: Three to four weeks after transplanting, cut the plants at the base with a sharp knife or pull them with the roots, in the cool early morning or late afternoon.

blocks.text: Sown straight on the bed, step by step
This is the sown straight on the bed way (Sown straight on the bed (sabog tanim)). The crop is ready about 35 days after sowing.
Sown straight on the bed: before planting (Bago magtanim)

items.title: 14 days before sowing: Prepare the beds
items.text: Plow, harrow and form beds about 1 m wide, then rake manure or compost into the top soil.

blocks.text: Sown straight on the bed: planting day (Pagtatanim)

items.title: Sowing day: Sow the seed
items.text: Broadcast the seed thinly over the bed, or drop it in shallow lines about 20 cm apart. Dust a little fine soil or rice hull over the seed and water gently.

blocks.text: Sown straight on the bed: care while it grows (Pag aalaga)

items.title: Day 1: Keep the bed moist
items.text: Sprinkle the bed every day until the seedlings are up, then water daily in the cool hours.

items.title: Day 12: Thin the seedlings
items.text: Pull out extra plants so the rest stand about 10 cm apart. The thinnings can be cooked or sold.

items.title: Day 15: Side dress and weed
items.text: Give a light side dressing of urea or manure tea and pull the weeds.

items.title: Day 18: Scout for leaf eaters
items.text: Check the leaves for flea beetle holes, aphids and diamondback moth larvae, and remove rotting plants.

blocks.text: Sown straight on the bed: harvest (Anihan)

items.title: Day 35: Harvest the whole plant
items.text: About 30 to 40 days after sowing, while the leaves are still tender, pull or cut the plants in the cool of the day.

blocks.text: Spacing, water and fertilizer for petsay
Spacing
Beds about 1 m wide with 20 to 25 cm paths. Plants 10 cm apart in rows 20 cm apart, one plant a hill. Direct sown beds are thinned to about the same.
Water

Watered by hand every day with a watering can or hose in the morning or late afternoon, right after transplanting and until harvest. Larger fields are watered by furrow. Beds must drain well. Standing water rots the plants.
Fertilizer

Traditional growers lean on chicken manure mixed into the beds, plus a little complete fertilizer (14 14 14) at planting and urea after one to two weeks. One common plot guide for a bed 1 m by 20 m is a sack of chicken manure, 1 kg of 14 14 14 and about 4 kg of urea worked into the soil before transplanting. To read what a bag really gives, see our guide to [fertilizer for this crop](/blog/fertilizer-for-vegetables-philippines).
Care and harvest
Care while it grows
Daily watering, one or two hand weedings, thinning of direct sown beds, and close watch for leaf eating insects. Seedlings get a light shade and are hardened for a week before transplanting.
When and how to harvest

Pechay is ready three to four weeks after transplanting, or 30 to 40 days after direct sowing, while the leaves are tender. Farmers cut the plant at the base or pull it with the roots in the cool hours, wash it, remove yellow leaves, tie it in bundles and keep it shaded and moist.
Common mistakes when planting petsay

items: Sowing too thick and never thinning, so the plants come out thin and weak.
Watering at noon or letting water stand in the beds, which scorches leaves or brings soft rot.
Planting pechay right after cabbage, mustard or other cabbage family crops on the same bed again and again, so club root and diamondback moth build up.
Flat, low beds in the rainy months.
Harvesting at midday in the heat, so the leaves wilt before they reach the market.

blocks.text: How to get a higher yield of petsay
The traditional way gets a crop, but small changes add up. These are the first things to change, one season at a time.

items: Buy fresh seed of a variety suited to the season, with heat or rain tolerance for the wet months.
Test the soil and lime acid soils. Feed by the result with compost plus balanced fertilizer.
Use raised beds and a mulch of rice straw or plastic to keep the leaves clean and the weeds down.
Rotate pechay with crops outside the cabbage family, such as beans, corn or squash.
Scout twice a week and protect the seedbed with a fine net against leaf eating insects.
Harvest in the cool hours and keep the bundles shaded and moist on the way to market.

blocks.text: Questions about planting petsay

items.q: When do farmers plant petsay in the Philippines?
items.a: Pechay grows all year in the lowlands but does best in the dry, cooler months, roughly November to April. In the rainy months farmers plant on raised beds and under light cover, because heavy rain tears the leaves and brings rot.

items.q: How far apart do you plant petsay?
items.a: Beds about 1 m wide with 20 to 25 cm paths. Plants 10 cm apart in rows 20 cm apart, one plant a hill.

items.q: How long before petsay can be harvested?
items.a: Seedbed then transplant, it is ready about 25 days after transplanting. Sown straight on the bed, it is ready about 35 days after sowing. Pechay is ready three to four weeks after transplanting, or 30 to 40 days after direct sowing, while the leaves are tender.

items.q: What do you plant to grow petsay?
items.a: Seed, bought in small packs or cans. Farmers either sow it thinly in a seedbed or seedling tray and transplant the seedlings after two to three weeks, or broadcast or drill it straight on the bed and thin later.
